w: The old Chain Pier collapsed in 1896 while its replacement was still being built -- an odd omen for the Palace Pier. Opened in 1899, it built a theatre and was Brighton's busiest venue by 1911. The theatre was demolished in 1986, and the pier reinvented itself as a fairground -- the version seen in Brighton Rock.
s: Its predecessor pier collapsed as this one rose
_facts: Opened 1899 as replacement for the Chain Pier, which collapsed in 1896 during the new pier's construction
A popular theatre and entertainment venue by 1911
Theatre damaged in 1973, demolished in 1986, shifting the pier to an amusement park
Featured in Brighton Rock, Carry On at Your Convenience, and The Who's Quadrophenia

w: Brighton's original parish church, standing on high ground above what's now the main shopping strip -- a quiet, older world just off the tourist route. Only two buildings in the city are older: St Helen's in Hangleton and St Peter's in Preston village. Everything else downhill from here came later.
s: Brighton's original, and third-oldest, parish church
_facts: The original parish church of Brighton
The third-oldest surviving building in Brighton and Hove, after St Helen's, Hangleton and St Peter's, Preston village
Sits on high ground at Church Street and Dyke Road, close to the main shopping area
Grade II* listed for its architectural significance

w: Two rejected designs and a year of wrangling produced this: a Tuscan column topped with a statue of Saint George gripping his sword by the blade, raised to the 600-plus Hove men killed in WWI. Edwin Lutyens picked the site but skipped the 1921 unveiling -- he was in India, and sent his office manager instead.
s: A Lutyens memorial the architect never saw unveiled
_facts: First World War memorial designed by Sir Edwin Lutyens, on Grand Avenue, Hove
Over 600 men from Hove were killed in the war
A Tuscan column topped with a statue of Saint George, cast in the studio of Sir George Frampton
Unveiled 27 February 1921; Lutyens was in India and was represented by his office manager
